result.summary: Adds test cases to `script_tests.json` and `feature_taproot.py` covering the 1,000-element stack size limit boundary in P2SH evaluation. The tests verify that a scriptSig leaving 1,000 items fails with `STACK_SIZE` because the P2SH scriptPubKey's 20-byte hash push becomes the 1,001st item, while 999 items succeeds. They also test the 1,000 and 1,001 item boundary during redeemScript execution.
result.problem: Existing test vectors omit coverage for the stack size boundary when the P2SH scriptPubKey executes on top of the scriptSig's stack. Alternative Bitcoin implementations (such as rbitcoin) that check the redeemScript hash directly without executing the scriptPubKey against the stack can accept invalid 1,000-item spends while still passing every existing test vector.
evidence: PR description: 'An implementation that checks the redeemScript hash without running the scriptPubKey accepts the 1,000-item spend. No existing vector leaves the scriptSig at this boundary, so such an implementation can pass every row.'
PR description: 'These were discovered by finding gaps in an alternate implementation (rbitcoin)'
result.changed_since_previous: Adds two test cases to `script_tests.json` covering the 1,000-element stack boundary during redeemScript evaluation itself.
result.card: Adds test cases to `script_tests.json` and `feature_taproot.py` covering the 1,000-element stack size boundary during P2SH and redeemScript evaluation. Existing test vectors do not exercise this boundary before the scriptPubKey runs, allowing alternative node implementations that check the redeemScript hash without executing the scriptPubKey to accept invalid 1,000-item spends while passing the entire test suite. Enables dumping the new spender transaction to QA script test assets (bitcoin-core/qa-assets#297).

risk.why: Only touches test data and test scripts; a mistake could cause test suite false positives or test failures, but cannot affect node consensus behavior or release binaries.
